designs.title: Pisa
designs.why: Clean one-ink line art that reads instantly from 3 m: a stamp silhouette, a big PISA and the tower. The tilted stamp with an upright tower, plus the 3.97° tag, is a smart quiet joke. Linework is solid, with no halftones and no hairlines that would drop out. The risk is the tower's arcade detail: arch, column and capital gaps run about 3-4 px (roughly 0.5-0.7 mm at print size), so they will fill in, especially white-on-black, where the underbase spreads and the eight galleries go muddy. The ground strip with its tiny bollards is fussy and adds nothing. The mockups also look less tilted than the art, so check the placement matches the file.
designs.fix: Simplify the tower's galleries (fewer, thicker columns and open arch counters of at least 1 mm, dropping the inner double-line arch rims) and build a separate choked version for the black tee, so the detail holds after ink spread.
